caption:
🚨 Meta just showed its Muse AI agent moving off your phone and onto your AI glasses.

Right now most smart glasses just take photos or play audio. Muse can actually see what you're looking at and act on it.

→ say its name and it acts on whatever you're looking at
→ fully hands-free, no phone, no typing
→ checks a flight, shops a shelf, books a table while you keep talking
→ new connectors this round: Walmart, Best Buy, Expedia, Instacart

Would you actually talk to your glasses like this, or does it feel too weird? 👇 Save this before Muse starts rolling out.

captions.facebook:
Meta just showed its Muse AI agent moving off your phone and onto your face.

At Connect 2026, Meta demoed Muse working through AI glasses: say its name, look at something, and it acts on it — no describing out loud, no typing.

In the demo it checked a flight price, shopped a shelf, and booked a table, all while the person kept talking. Meta says the rollout starts in the coming months.

Would you want an AI agent watching through your glasses, or does that cross a line for you?

slides.title: Meta's Muse AI agent is coming to your AI glasses.
slides.sub: Say its name, look at what you're looking at, and it acts — hands stay free.
slides.voiceover: Meta just said its Muse AI agent is coming to your smart glasses.

slides.label: WHAT MUSE DOES
slides.title: Not a voice assistant you describe things to
items: Say Muse's name and it acts on whatever you're looking at, no describing needed
Muse keeps working on a task while you're still talking about something else
No phone, no typing — the whole interaction is voice plus your glasses' camera
New connectors this round: Walmart, Best Buy, Expedia, Instacart, Notion, GitHub
slides.voiceover: Say Muse's name, look at something, and it acts — no describing, no typing.

slides.label: SEEING WHAT YOU SEE
slides.title: Three things Meta showed it doing
steps: Look at a product or a flier and ask Muse to check it or add it to your list
Ask about a price or a booking while Muse looks through your glasses with you
Muse can act on a request in the background without breaking your conversation
slides.voiceover: Look at a shelf, a flier, a flight price — Muse can act on what it sees.

slides.label: OLD VS. NEW
slides.title: How this differs from a normal voice assistant

cols.name: Typical voice assistant
points: You describe what you see out loud
One command, one answer, then it stops
Can't hold a task while you keep talking

cols.name: Muse on glasses
points: It already sees what you're looking at
Keeps a long, in-depth conversation going
Finishes tasks in the background as you talk

slides.voiceover: A normal assistant waits for a command. Muse sees, and keeps working while you talk.

slides.label: TIMELINE
slides.title: When Muse reaches AI glasses
slides.sub: Meta says the rollout starts in the coming months and expands through 2026, alongside 100+ AI glasses options by year-end.
slides.voiceover: Meta says Muse starts rolling out to AI glasses in the coming months.

slides.label: WORTH KNOWING
slides.title: This isn't the audio-only Ray-Ban launch
items: Different from the earlier Ray-Ban Meta audio glasses news — this is agent software, not new hardware
Meta hasn't named which specific glasses get Muse first
"Coming months" is Meta's own wording — no fixed date yet
slides.voiceover: This is the agent, not new hardware — and Meta hasn't fixed an exact date yet.

slides.title: Hands-free AI
lines: Muse rolling out on AI glasses in the coming months
